title: Billing the Drug Plan Premium and the Late Enrollment Penalty on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
The plan bills the drug plan premium of the Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan held for each coverage month from the coverage effective date to the coverage end date, split into its basic and supplemental components so that each can be relieved on its own. The amount billed for a coverage month is the basic premium portion of the plan held together with its supplemental premium portion.

A charge is posted only while the enrollment is in force or in its premium grace period on the day the charge is posted; the enrollment's own status on that day is what settles it.

## How the components are billed

1. The late enrollment penalty is billed as its own component of the same coverage month, never folded into the premium, because the two are relieved by different events and a member may owe one without the other.
2. Where CMS has told the plan that a low-income subsidy applies, the full premium is still charged and the subsidy is posted separately as a credit, so the member can see what the plan charged and what the subsidy paid.
3. A quarterly billing frequency bills three coverage months in one charge posted in the first of those months, and what is owed for a coverage month never changes with the frequency.
4. No premium or penalty is charged for a coverage month beginning after the coverage end date, and a charge already posted for such a month is relieved by a credit rather than left outstanding.

## Basis Q&A

**On what footing is a quarterly-billed member charged for a coverage month?** On exactly the footing a monthly-billed member is charged. Three coverage months are gathered into one charge posted in the first of them, but the amount owed for each of those months is the same premium the plan held gives.

**Where a subsidy applies, is the premium charged net of it?** No. The full premium is charged and the subsidy is posted as a separate credit against it.

**May a penalty be charged for a coverage month that begins after coverage ended?** No. Neither premium nor penalty is charged for such a month, and a charge already posted for one is relieved by a credit.
